heading: 8.5 Unit assertion function
text:
### 8.5 Unit assertion function [LUNI.8.5]

Asserting a number into a unit type and stripping a unit back to a number are
`::` conversion casts ([LCST.4.5.2]). The number is of the kind the unit's
dimension stores ([LUNI.8.7.3]): `Float` for a `float64` dimension, `Int` for an
`int64` or `int32` one. Both casts are total and zero-cost (identity at runtime,
compile-time type annotation only): `<number> → <unit>` asserts the dimension
tag without applying the affine factor, and `<unit> → <number>` strips it. The
strip applies to a unit-typed value and a dimension-typed value ([LUNI.7.1])
alike, and yields the stored base-unit number. A source of any other kind, such
as a `String` asserted into a unit, has no conversion and is refused as an
undefined pair ([LCST.4.5.3]).

Assigning a number to a unit-typed field without the `::<unit>` assertion is a
compiler error; the message suggests the cast form.
